{{Quote|But somebody has to do it, and I'm that somebody. I didn't choose it &mdash; it was chosen for me, when the jacks came to Okator.|Baragwin sense lattice imprinted by the Republic soldier|<ref name="Author's Cut" />}}
A [[Gender/Legends|male]] '''individual''' lived during the final [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of the [[Tionese War]], which was fought between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Honorable Union of Desevro and Tion|Honorable Union of Desevro & Tion]] from [[24,000 BBY]] to [[23,900 BBY]]. Growing up on [[Little Atullus]], as a [[Youngling/Legends|boy]] they moved with their [[Parent/Legends|parents]] to [[Okator VIII]], where they had purchased a [[Unidentified farm (Okator VIII)|land property]]. The family established a [[Farm/Legends|farm]] there, keeping a herd of local [[Whellay/Legends|whellays]] and growing several types of [[Plant/Legends|plants]]. The boy [[Farmer/Legends|helped]] at the farm, shepherding the whellays with the assistance of several [[shakwulf]]s. They eventually got used to, and then became happy with, the busy pastoral life.

[[Standard month/Legends|Months]] before the end of the Tionese War, however, the boy's life changed when a group of [[Tionese (group)/Legends|Tionese]] [[Tionjack|warships]] [[Attack on Okator VIII|arrived]] at Okator VIII with the intention of destroying the local Republic settlements. Away from the farm at the [[Time/Legends|time]], the boy witnessed the decimation of several inhabited locations before finally rushing back home before it, too, could be destroyed. They were too late, as one of the [[Warship/Legends|warships]] set the farm on [[Fire/Legends|fire]], with the boy helplessly observing the destruction of their home and the [[Death/Legends|death]] of their family's whellays and their favorite shakwulf, [[Brun (shakwulf)|Brun]].

[[Standard week/Legends|Weeks]] later, the boy traveled to the Republic [[Planet/Legends|world]] [[Abhean/Legends|Abhean]] to enlist with the [[Republic Military/Legends|Republic Military]]. Mere months after the former farm-boy became a [[Republic soldier]], the Tionese War ended, and they eventually became assigned to the Republic [[Fortress world/Legends|fortress world]] [[Falang Minor]]. There, the [[Soldier/Legends|soldier]] monitored starship traffic, intelligence, and transmissions originating in the [[Tion Cluster/Legends|Tion Cluster]]. After having served on Falang Minor for twelve years, the soldier recorded an account of the attack on Okator VIII that they imprinted on a [[Baragwin sense lattice]], with the record being kept in the [[Palace of Memnii]] on [[Caamas/Legends|Caamas]] twenty [[Millennium/Legends|thousand years]] later.

==Biography==
===Early childhood===
{{Quote|I grew up on Little Atullus, but my parents brought me to Okator VIII when I was a boy.|Baragwin sense lattice imprinted by the Republic soldier|<ref name="Author's Cut" />}}
[[File:PerlemianCorridor22kBBY-TEA.jpg|thumb|right|300px|The Republic soldier spent their childhood on Okator VIII (situated between Abhean and [[Roche]] in the red-colored territory).]]
During the [[Tionese War]],<ref name="Author's Cut" /> which was fought between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Honorable Union of Desevro and Tion|Honorable Union of Desevro & Tion]]<ref name="EGTW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> for roughly a [[Standard century/Legends|century]] beginning in [[24,000 BBY]],<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> a [[Gender/Legends|boy]] was [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] into a family living as part of the Republic on the<ref name="Author's Cut" /> [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim]]<ref name="EAOC Little Atullus">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}} &mdash; Based on corresponding data for [[Little Atullus system/Legends|Little Atullus system]]</ref> astronomical object [[Little Atullus]]. At some point, the [[Youngling/Legends|boy's]] [[Parent/Legends|parents]] invested their life savings into a land property on [[the Divide]] celestial body [[Okator VIII]] that was offered by a group of [[Merchant/Legends|traders]] from<ref name="Author's Cut" /> the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="TEA" /> [[Brentaal IV/Legends|Brentaal]]. The boy and their parents eventually left Little Atullus for Okator VIII, where they began to establish a [[Unidentified farm (Okator VIII)|farm]] in a valley.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

The boy's first job, while their parents built a cabin and cleared out fields, was to capture the local creatures known as [[Whellay/Legends|whellays]] by putting out bait in Okator VIII's [[Forest/Legends|forests]]. On the first [[Standard day/Legends|day]], the boy caught six of the creatures and gave each of them a name, with their parents having neglected to tell them the whellays were meant for the family to [[Foodstuff/Legends|cook]] and [[Diet/Legends|eat]].<ref name="Author's Cut" />

===A farmer's life===
{{Quote|I was lonely at first, but eventually I forgot about Little Atullus, except in dreams. And I got used to farm life.|Baragwin sense lattice imprinted by the soldier|<ref name="Author's Cut" />}}
Eventually the boy settled into the busy life at the [[Farm/Legends|farm]]. The family [[Farmer/Legends|kept]] a herd of whellays, and the boy was entrusted with shepherding them with the assistance of domesticated [[shakwulf]]s. The boy would let the whellays, tended by a shakwulf, out at dawn and then signal the creature to bring the herd back home after lunch. The following afternoon was usually spent in grooming the [[Hair/Legends|coats]] of the whellays and checking their hooves as well as monitoring the creatures for signs of coming into estrus and researching their [[Book/Legends|lineage-books]] to determine the best pairings. In shearing season, the boy would stay in the barn into the night helping out their parents with the whellays.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

Besides helping maintain the whellay herd, the boy's morning duties included tending the several types of [[Plant/Legends|plants]] the family was growing. The boy weeded [[saria]], harvested [[Nectar/Legends|nectar]] from [[charsby]] orchards, and tapped loam for ripe [[galt-gourd]]s. In the evening, the family ate dinner, after which the boy was occupied with repairs and lessons. From [[Time/Legends|time]] to time, the boy and their family went to [[City/Legends|town]], where they would hear the latest news on the progress of the Tionese War.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

===The Tionese attack===
{{Quote|I was out in the forests with Brun tracking a lost whellay when I heard the first ship. ''[&hellip;]'' I didn't see that one, but I saw the next one, and the third. They were copper-colored, with red sigils on the conning towers, and I knew they were Tionjacks.|Baragwin sense lattice imprinted by the soldier|<ref name="Author's Cut" />}}
[[Standard month/Legends|Months]] before the war's end<ref name="Author's Cut" /> around [[23,900 BBY]],<ref name="TEA" /> the boy, accompanied by their favorite shakwulf, [[Brun (shakwulf)|Brun]], was tracking down a lost whellay in Okator VIII's forests when they witnessed the [[Attack on Okator VIII|arrival]] of a group of [[Tionese (group)/Legends|Tionese]] [[Tionjack|warships]] intent on destroying the Republic settlements on the celestial body. The boy heard the approach of one [[Warship/Legends|warship]] and then saw two additional [[Starship/Legends|vessels]]. One of the ships destroyed [[Derway Township]] by detonating a [[pressure bomb]], and the explosion knocked the boy to the ground and temporarily disabled their hearing.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

Acting on their training to protect the whellay herd from any danger, Brun ran back toward the farm. After the boy observed the Tionese decimation of [[Duny Gap]] and [[Shillagh Hollow]] settlements, they noticed a warship hovering over the farm and followed Brun. They arrived just in time to watch the farm, including the animals and plants there, being set on [[Fire/Legends|fire]] by the Tionese vessel's attack run, after which the warships left Okator VIII.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

===A soldier for the Republic===
{{Quote|And now I've been here for 12 years. A Republic Guardsman, serving the Jedi watchmen.|Baragwin sense lattice imprinted by the soldier|<ref name="Author's Cut" />}}
[[File:FalangMinor-TEA.jpg|thumb|left|300px|On Falang Minor, the soldier helped the Republic monitor the Tion Cluster.]]
Five [[Standard week/Legends|weeks]] after the Tionese attack, the boy was able to hail a [[Scout ship/Legends|scoutship]] that allowed them to leave their adopted [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] forever. Although they were encouraged to talk about their experience on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]],<ref name="Author's Cut" /> the [[Capital/Legends|capital]] world of the Republic,<ref name="TEA" /> the boy refused and instead traveled to<ref name="Author's Cut" /> the Republic world<ref name="EGTW" /> [[Abhean/Legends|Abhean]] to enlist with the [[Republic Military/Legends|Republic Military]].<ref name="Author's Cut" />

Eventually the young man was made a [[Republic soldier]]. Four months later, however, before they could join the fight against the Tionese, the war ended in a victory for the Republic. The [[Soldier/Legends|soldier]] was eventually assigned to [[Falang Minor]],<ref name="Author's Cut" /> one of a series of Republic [[Fortress world/Legends|fortress worlds]] established<ref name="GatORW">''[[Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds]]''</ref> along the Coreward boundaries of the [[Tion Cluster/Legends|Tion Cluster]].<ref name="EGTW" /> Placed under the [[Commanding officer/Legends|command]] of [[Jedi Watchman/Legends|watchmen]] of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]], the soldier's duties included monitoring starship traffic, intelligence, and transmissions originating in the [[Star cluster/Legends|star cluster]]. After having served on Falang Minor for twelve [[Standard year/Legends|years]], the soldier imprinted an anonymous audio-visual account on a [[Baragwin sense lattice]]. They recorded a brief narration of their early life as well as an account of the Tionese attack on Okator VIII.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

The sense lattice containing the soldier's narration eventually became one of the oldest records preserved in the [[Palace of Memnii]] on<ref name="Author's Cut" /> the planet<ref name="Coruscant">''[[Coruscant and the Core Worlds]]''</ref> [[Caamas/Legends|Caamas]]. Although the structure was [[Caamas Firestorm|destroyed]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], at least one copy of the soldier's account remained intact in the possession of a traveling [[Memnis|memnii]] exhibit.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

==Personality and traits==
===Happy farmer===
{{Quote|At first I only tolerated ''[the life at the farm]''. Then I realized I was happy.|Baragwin sense lattice imprinted by the soldier|<ref name="Author's Cut" />}}
Regarding their original homeworld of Little Atullus, the boy who would later become a Republic soldier noted that they partially agreed with the sentiment prevalent there during their childhood&mdash;that [[Colonist/Legends|colonists]] could lead better lives on the worlds beyond the region known as the Rim. The boy characterized the traders who sold their parents a land property on one such celestial body, Okator VIII, as "hotshot."<ref name="Author's Cut" />

[[File:Hutt_warrior_TEGTW.jpg|thumb|right|300px|The soldier referred to the Hutts (pictured) as "devil-slugs."]]
After their family moved to Okator VIII, the boy initially felt lonely but eventually got used to life at a farm. Over time, they forgot about Little Atullus, only continuing to see it in their [[Dream/Legends|dreams]]. At first the boy only tolerated their daily routine, resenting the fact that they had to take lessons after a day of working at the farm. At some point, however, they realized that they were happy with their new life, with their contentment fueled by their intense familiarity with their environment. When they caught six whellays on their first day of luring the creatures in by putting out food in the woods, the boy imagined that they were a [[Deity/Legends|god]] of the forest. The boy knew the shakwulf named Brun from the creature's first moments as a [[Eye/Legends|blind]] pup. Brun became the boy's favorite shakwulf companion, and the latter was confident the former loved them more than anything else in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="Author's Cut" />

During their childhood, the Republic soldier was aware of atrocities the Tionese had committed against the Republic, as well as the possibility that the Republic had reciprocated. Ultimately, however, the boy was convinced that Okator VIII's remoteness from the Tion Cluster rendered the threat of war irrelevant to their adopted homeworld,<ref name="Author's Cut" /> despite the fact that at the beginning of the conflict, the Tionese had penetrated the Republic's territory as far as the Core Worlds.<ref name="EGTW" /> In addition, the boy believed that [[Xim/Legends|Xim]],<ref name="Author's Cut" /> the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Emperor/Legends|ruler]] of a large [[Xim's empire|interstellar empire]] centered in the Tion Cluster who had [[Death/Legends|died]] more than a [[Millennium/Legends|thousand years]] earlier after being [[Third Battle of Vontor|defeated]] in a [[Xim Wars|war]] against the [[Hutt Empire|empire]] of the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Species/Legends|species]]<ref name="EGTW" /> and the location and circumstances of whose death later [[Scholar/Legends|scholars]] disagreed on,<ref name="Xim">{{SW|url=news/essential-atlas-extra-the-history-of-xim-and-the-tion-cluster|text=Essential Atlas Extra: The History of Xim and the Tion Cluster|int=Xim Week: The History of Xim and the Tion Cluster}}</ref> had been eaten by the Hutts. The boy referred to the Hutts as "[[Demon/Legends|devil]]-[[Slug (creature)/Legends|slugs]]" and believed they had consumed Xim in order to obtain his supposed powers.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

===A survivor===
{{Quote|I don't hate the Tionese anymore. I used to. It made me feel sick all the time, so I made myself stop. But I don't trust them. No one in the Republic should ever trust them.|Baragwin sense lattice imprinted by the soldier|<ref name="Author's Cut" />}}
After witnessing the destruction of their family's farm during the Tionese attack on Okator VIII, the soldier came to believe that the worst thing about the experience was the fact that they had arrived at the farm in time to see it immediately before its decimation. As a result, they had noticed that Brun had brought their whellay herd back home&mdash;which proved to be the creature's doom. As the boy witnessed the animals being set on fire by the attack, their resultant suffering seemed excessively long to them, and they only wished that the creatures would stand still so as to quicken their death.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

Following the attack, the boy turned down the suggestion of telling their story at the Republic's capital, instead opting to enlist with that government's military for a chance to fight the Tionese who had destroyed their home. The war's end denied the soldier that chance, and eventually they were posted on Falang Minor, where they helped monitor the Tion Cluster. They disliked that world's barren nature and harsh climate, and they also lamented the passive nature of their assignment, which gave them too many opportunities for introspection. Although the soldier initially hated the Tionese for their deeds, that disposition made them constantly feel sick, and they let go of the hatred.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

Ultimately, however, the soldier felt that it was their duty to perform their responsibilities, believing that they were chosen for the task when the Tionese warships arrived to destroy the Okator VIII settlements. The soldier deeply distrusted the people who had destroyed their home and believed that everyone in the Republic should forever share that distrust. In an account of the attack on Okator VIII recorded after having served on Falang Minor for twelve years, the soldier's grim attitude toward the Tionese led them to express their conviction that Republic agents on that world would always keep monitoring the Tion Cluster.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

==Skills and abilities==
{{Quote|I monitor ship traffic, intelligence, transmissions &mdash; everything that comes out of the Tion.|Baragwin sense lattice imprinted by the soldier|<ref name="Author's Cut" />}}
During the time they spent in their family's farm as a boy, the Republic soldier became well-acquainted with their surroundings. They could recognize individual [[Tree/Legends|trees]] in the forests surrounding the farm; every outcropping in the nearby hills; and every depression and ridge of the farm's orchards. Over time, the boy also learned to recognize each of their family's whellays by their individual smell and whicker.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

In addition, the boy became familiar with the sounds made by the [[Engine/Legends|engines]] of [[tradeship]]s and [[Courier/Legends|courier]] starships regularly visiting Okator VIII. That familiarity allowed them to instantly realize the foreign nature of the Tionese warships that had arrived to destroy the local settlements, and the boy's knowledge of the Tionese War allowed them to specifically recognize the warships as Tionjacks upon sight. During his service in the Republic Military, the soldier acquired the skills necessary to perform their duties, which included monitoring starship traffic, intelligence, and transmissions.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|I created Uthtara as part of a first-person remembrance of a Tionese attack on a Republic frontier world. I had to cut the vignette ''[...]''.|Jason Fry|<ref name="Tumblr">{{Tumblr|subdomain=jasonfry|url=post/20907109370/eg-to-warfare-endnotes-pt-2|name=Jason Fry's Dorkery|text=EG to Warfare: Endnotes Pt. 2}}</ref>}}
The unnamed Republic soldier was originally meant to serve as the narrator of an [[in-universe]] section in the [[2012]] reference book ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' by [[Jason Fry]] and [[Paul R. Urquhart]]; however, the section,<ref name="Author's Cut" /> titled "A Soldier's Story: Lights in the Darkness,"<ref name="Outline">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-part-12-tales-of-the-new-republic|series=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|text=Part 12: Tales of the New Republic}}</ref> was cut before the book's release. The section, which both Fry and<ref name="Author's Cut" /> [[Del Rey]] editor<ref name="Celestials">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-the-celestials|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare'' Author's Cut &mdash; The Celestials|int=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut}}</ref> [[Erich Schoeneweiss]] characterized as "poignant" and which Fry further described as "one of my favorite bits of writing that wound up on the cutting-room floor," was later renamed "The Watchman's Tale" and was released in [[2014]] as part of [[Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|''Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare'' Author's Cut]], a series of articles published on the [[StarWars.com]] [[Star Wars Blog|Blog]] containing various cut content from ''The Essential Guide to Warfare''.<ref name="Author's Cut" />
